Provider-backed Razorpay Test Mode acceptance now includes successful captures, signed webhook delivery, browser confirmation, acknowledgement creation, exact appeal accounting and a full refund. On 2026-09-19 the INR 110 test payment `pay_Tdo33NThi9m4rH` was refunded from the Razorpay Test Dashboard; Razorpay delivered `refund.processed` to `/api/webhooks/razorpay` with HTTP 200, Neon changed donation `AFD-2026-52467908` from CAPTURED to REFUNDED, set `refundedAmount` to INR 110 and `refundedAt`, and the staging acceptance appeal reconciled from INR 310 back to INR 200. During repeated checkout testing, a real client-side regression was found where revisiting the donation page after Razorpay had already loaded could leave the button stuck on `Preparing secure checkout…` until a hard refresh. The quiet branch fixes this by using Next Script `onReady` plus an already-loaded `window.Razorpay` mount check, with a browser-acceptance remount regression added. Provider-backed `payment.failed` evidence remains pending because the current Razorpay Test Checkout did not expose the documented Success/Failure controls in the observed Netbanking/Wallet/UPI flows; the route-level failed-payment state guards now have explicit automated coverage. Live-mode acceptance and production email delivery remain pending.

Domain control, Cloudflare TLS and DNS ownership are verified. As of 2026-09-19 `amaanafoundation.org` is intentionally attached to the Railway family/staging service `amaana-rebuild-preview`, while a separate `amaana-platform` service sourced from `main` exists with only a Railway-generated domain. Final production cutover must deliberately move the official custom domain to `amaana-platform` only after the approved release and production-only variables are ready; staging must retain Test Razorpay credentials.

The real domain is reachable directly, but indexing remains intentionally fail-closed. Indexing now requires the explicit flag, the official HTTPS Amaana host, and APP_ENVIRONMENT=production; the Docker build defaults APP_ENVIRONMENT to staging and receives the environment at build time. A future approved indexing decision therefore requires a deliberate production rebuild with APP_ENVIRONMENT=production and NEXT_PUBLIC_ALLOW_INDEXING=true, followed by robots/sitemap/canonical verification. Runtime-only flag changes cannot make a staging-built image indexable.
Merging to main and formal production release approval remain explicitly user-gated actions.
